milestones.title: M0 - v0.1 Reproducible foundation
milestones.description: Ship the offline compiler, policy engine, scenario families, provenance, resumable builds, training exports, document compiler, and single-step task exporter. Acceptance: end-to-end example, regression tests, lint, typing, documentation and package builds pass.

milestones.title: M1 - v0.2 Organization compiler
milestones.description: Build source adapters, span-level evidence, rule review, workflow extraction evaluation, and resumable compilation for larger corpora. Acceptance: source locations and access metadata are preserved; reviewed fixtures measure extraction quality; conflicts enter a review queue.

milestones.title: M2 - v0.3 Distribution-aware synthesis
milestones.description: Integrate conditional generation, sampling budgets, scenario-family transformations, persistent orchestration, and bounded model usage. Acceptance: requested versus realized distributions, recovery tests, and per-accepted-example cost reports.

milestones.title: M3 - v0.4 Executable organization tasks
milestones.description: Run multi-step organizational tasks with mock business tools and independent graders through supported harnesses. Acceptance: resettable environments, protected grading inputs, separate utility/compliance/cost metrics, and multiple harness/model configurations.

milestones.title: M4 - v0.5 Feedback and targeted updates
milestones.description: Connect runtime events and reviewed outcomes to source-to-model lineage and targeted regeneration. Acceptance: changed policies identify affected artifacts, unchanged artifacts are reused, test families stay isolated, and update quality/cost is reproducible.

milestones.title: M5 - v1.0 Stable open-source platform
milestones.description: Stabilize APIs, migrations, operational guidance, performance evaluation, and release automation. Acceptance: supported adapter compatibility matrix, clean-system reproduction, documented benchmarks, and a public deprecation policy.

issues.title: Implement typed contracts and the verified offline data pipeline
issues.body:
Deliver the first complete data path.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Typed organization, rule, node, recipe, and episode contracts.
- [x] Exact evidence validation and deterministic policy decisions.
- [x] Family split isolation, cache integrity, source hashes, and change analysis.
- [x] Offline example and regression tests.

issues.title: Ship document compilation, training exports, and portable decision tasks
issues.body:
Provide usable interfaces around the data core.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Explicit JSON Schema-capable model provider.
- [x] Canonical, typed-choice, and chat SFT exports.
- [x] Offline decision replay and Harbor single-step task export.
- [x] CLI error handling and integration tests.

issues.title: Establish documentation, CI, governance, and release packaging
issues.body:
Prepare an English-only open-source foundation.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Architecture, data protocol, specification, and contribution documentation.
- [x] Apache-2.0 license, security policy, and community guidelines.
- [x] Lint, typing, test, documentation, and package-build automation.
- [x] Machine-readable milestones and idempotent publication tooling.

issues.title: Add source adapter contracts with document spans and access metadata
issues.body:
Support larger document collections through a stable ingestion interface.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Define source version, span, permission, and content-hash contracts.
- [x] Implement PDF and structured workflow adapters with fixtures.
- [x] Preserve page/section references through compilation.
- [x] Verify unchanged source reuse and changed-source invalidation.

Implementation evidence: source/PDF/workflow fixtures, content-bound review regression tests, and reproducible flagship model artifacts in experiments/2026-10-m1. References are maintainer-authored and independently code-reviewed; broader expert-annotated corpus acceptance remains tracked in M1.

issues.title: Build a policy review queue and independent extraction evaluation
issues.body:
Give business reviewers a concrete rule-and-evidence review surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Track proposed, accepted, rejected, and conflicting interpretations.
- [x] Compare extracted rules with independently reviewed fixtures.
- [x] Record reviewer decisions and policy-version lineage.
- [x] Export review summaries without leaking private source content.

Implementation evidence: source/PDF/workflow fixtures, content-bound review regression tests, and reproducible flagship model artifacts in experiments/2026-10-m1. References are maintainer-authored and independently code-reviewed; broader expert-annotated corpus acceptance remains tracked in M1.

issues.title: Implement resumable corpus compilation and workflow reconstruction
issues.body:
Scale source analysis beyond a single model request.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Add chunk retrieval and cross-document rule resolution.
- [x] Resume completed extraction stages after interruption.
- [x] Enforce token/call budgets and record usage.
- [x] Evaluate decision-node recall and reference correctness.

Current implementation: overlapping source chunks, shared validated caches, bounded global claim assembly, checkpointed validation repairs, call/request-byte budgets, per-request output-token limits, and returned usage/cost. Larger multi-document interaction studies and retrieval-based rule resolution remain open.

Current implementation evidence: Aggregate token reservations now include request bytes and output caps. This conservative bound assumes byte-based text tokenization; actual returned usage and unknown attempts are retained. Cross-document retrieval/interaction acceptance remains open.

issues.title: Integrate a version-pinned NeMo Data Designer generation adapter
issues.body:
Compile Forge recipes to a dependency-aware generation backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Optional installation leaves the offline core dependency-light.
- [ ] Map scenario fields, constraints, validators, and artifact metadata.
- [x] Contract tests pin the supported backend version.
- [x] Resume tests and per-record generation cost reports pass.

Current implementation evidence: Data Designer 0.9.7 executes ordered seed expression processing with real SDK resume tests and zero model-call cost. Model-written scenario synthesis and backend conditional generation remain open; this adapter does not imply their completion.

issues.title: Add stratum budgets and constrained decision-family transformations
issues.body:
Make organization-specific training distributions explicit.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Configure routine, boundary, change, and development-feedback budgets.
- [x] Check feasibility and expected answer relationships after transformations.
- [ ] Add semantics-preserving rewrites and duplicate detection.
- [x] Report requested, generated, filtered, and accepted distributions.

issues.title: Add a persistent recipe-planning agent and tool registry
issues.body:
Expose discoverable typed tools for analysis, planning, previews, and execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Add a LangGraph adapter with durable stage state.
- [x] Store artifacts outside conversational working memory.
- [ ] Recover from provider failure without duplicate publication.
- [x] Route interpretation conflicts to the review queue.

Current implementation evidence: LangGraph 1.2.19 and SQLite checkpoint 3.1.3 persist review/build/export stages. Recipe-planning agent tools and provider-failure campaign acceptance remain open.

issues.title: Build the multi-step customer workflow environment
issues.body:
Exercise all four decision surfaces in one business task.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Provide mock CRM, information-sharing, approval, and acceptance tools.
- [x] Record decision-time state and subsequent transitions.
- [x] Reset the initial snapshot reproducibly.
- [x] Cover successful, blocked, escalated, and revised workflows.

Current implementation evidence: Implemented in workflows.py with three fictional task fixtures. Local live Opus 5.5/GPT-6.1 Sol runs are archived in experiments/2026-10-workflows. Container acceptance is tracked separately.

issues.title: Isolate workflow graders and validate them with mutation fixtures
issues.body:
Make executable labels independently checkable.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Run graders separately from solver-visible artifacts.
- [x] Validate positive, negative, and boundary cases.
- [x] Detect intentionally mutated permission and threshold checks.
- [x] Separate grader failures from agent failures.

Current implementation evidence: Independent trace replay recalculates permission, transition and utility. Mutation fixtures alter permission and state claims; solver failures and trace validity are reported separately.

issues.title: Run workflow tasks across Harbor harnesses and model configurations
issues.body:
Provide repeatable system-level evaluation.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Pin and test the Harbor runtime contract.
- [ ] Run at least two harness/model configurations on identical tasks.
- [ ] Record utility, compliance, cost, latency, and escalation separately.
- [ ] Document a Verifiers adapter decision based on integration needs.

issues.title: Define runtime event ingestion and decision-outcome association
issues.body:
Connect deployed decision calls to observable workflow results.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Version decision, action, tool-result, review, and outcome events.
- [x] Associate events using stable workflow and decision IDs.
- [x] Preserve observational versus verified label distinctions.
- [ ] Evaluate Agent Lightning capture without coupling typed heads to token RL.

issues.title: Extend impact analysis to span-level lineage and targeted regeneration
issues.body:
Update decision data when organizational policies change.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Track source spans through rules, tasks, datasets, and models.
- [x] Rebuild affected families and reuse unchanged artifacts.
- [ ] Test policy-version responsiveness and rollback provenance.
- [x] Measure update cost and verification outcomes.

Current implementation evidence: Cumulative family registry protects removed/restored held-out families; document-level source invalidation remains in use. Fine-grained span reuse and model-weight lineage remain open.

issues.title: Use reviewed development feedback to update generation priorities
issues.body:
Close the data improvement loop while preserving evaluation independence.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Convert development errors into traceable generation requests.
- [x] Keep test families outside adaptive generation.
- [ ] Compare recipes under fixed training budgets.
- [ ] Publish coverage, quality, and cost deltas per dataset version.

issues.title: Stabilize extension contracts, schema migrations, and compatibility policy
issues.body:
Prepare a maintainable public platform API.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Publish supported source, generator, verifier, exporter, and harness interfaces.
- [ ] Add schema migration fixtures and compatibility tests.
- [ ] Define release, support, and deprecation policies.
- [ ] Document third-party adapter development.

issues.title: Publish reproducible scale, quality, and cost benchmarks
issues.body:
Measure practical performance under documented conditions.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Report hardware, versions, source sizes, and sampling recipes.
- [x] Measure throughput, recovery, storage, and accepted-example cost.
- [ ] Report independent label review and downstream model quality.
- [ ] Reproduce results on clean systems.

Current implementation evidence: Measured cold/warm 2,800- and 28,000-episode offline builds, with script and hardware metadata. This measures data-pipeline execution; downstream training quality remains unmeasured.

issues.title: Establish signed releases, package publishing, and deployment guidance
issues.body:
Make project releases easy to adopt and verify.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Publish signed or attested release artifacts through controlled workflows.
- [ ] Configure trusted package publishing and provenance.
- [ ] Add operational deployment and backup/restore guidance.
- [ ] Validate installation and upgrades from published artifacts.
